summary: At twelve, Jesus stays behind in the temple after Passover, and when His anxious parents find Him, He speaks of being about His Father’s business.
key_insight: Mary said, “Your father and I have sought You.” Jesus answered with “My Father’s business.” In His first recorded words, the twelve-year-old names God as His Father. Then He went home with Joseph and Mary and was subject to them.
story: Every year Joseph and Mary went up to Jerusalem for the Feast of the Passover. When Jesus was twelve years old, they went up as usual, according to the custom of the feast.

When the days of the feast were over and they started home, the Boy Jesus lingered behind in Jerusalem, and Joseph and His mother did not know it. Supposing Him to be in the company, they traveled a full day before they looked for Him among their relatives and acquaintances. When they did not find Him, they went back to Jerusalem, searching for Him.

After three days they found Him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the teachers, both listening to them and asking them questions. All who heard Him were astonished at His understanding and answers.
His parents were amazed when they saw Him, and His mother said to Him, “Son, why have You done this to us? Look, Your father and I have sought You anxiously.”
He said to them, “Why did you seek Me? Did you not know that I must be about My Father’s business?” But they did not understand what He meant.
Then He went down with them to Nazareth and was subject to them. His mother kept all these things in her heart. And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and men.

scene.label: The Passover journey
scene.text: The law called the men of Israel to appear before the Lord at three feasts each year (Deuteronomy 16:16). Nazareth was roughly seventy miles from Jerusalem, several days on foot. Galileans traveled in large companies of relatives and neighbors, so a twelve-year-old could be out of sight for a day without alarm.

scene.label: Twelve years old
scene.text: Later Jewish writings set thirteen as the age when a boy took on the full duties of the law. At twelve, Jesus stood at the edge of that step.

scene.label: Among the teachers
scene.text: Teachers of the law met with students in the temple courts during the feasts. Students sat, listened and asked questions, and answering a teacher’s questions was part of learning. Jesus was taking part as a learner, and His answers amazed them.

scene.label: “After three days”
scene.text: Counting part-days as days, as people then did, this was probably one day’s travel out, one day back, and a day of searching in the crowded city.

scene.label: “My Father’s business”
scene.text: Jesus’ Greek phrase is brief and can mean either the affairs of His Father or the house of His Father. The NKJV reads “business”; many translations read “house.” Either way Jesus claims God as His Father, and they found Him in the temple.

witnesses.luke: Luke alone records any event from Jesus’ boyhood, and he shows a real boy who grows (2:40, 52) yet already knows who His Father is. Luke’s Gospel begins in the temple (1:9) and ends there (24:53), and between them the Boy Jesus sits in the temple among the teachers. Twice Luke says Mary kept these things in her heart (2:19, 51), a hint of where he learned them.

seeing.reveals: Even as a boy, Jesus knew His unique relationship with God as His Father. He also lived as a real son in a real home, learning, obeying and growing.
seeing.living: Jesus was sure of His Father’s claim on Him, and He went home and obeyed Joseph and Mary. Devotion to God showed itself in faithful duty at home. Mary did not understand His words, yet she kept them in her heart; when Jesus’ words puzzle you, hold on to them rather than set them aside.
seeing.ponder: Is there something Jesus has said that you do not yet understand, which you need to keep in your heart instead of setting aside?

preaching.big_idea: Jesus belonged first to His Father, and that made Him a faithful Son at home.
outline: A lost Son found in His Father’s house (43–47)
A question that reveals who He is (48–50)
A Son who obeys and grows (51–52)
preaching.watch_for: The word “must” in verse 49 is the first of many in Luke: “I must preach the kingdom of God” (4:43), “The Son of Man must suffer” (9:22), and “all things must be fulfilled” (24:44). From boyhood, Jesus lives under His Father’s purpose.
